narrativeProgression.description: Introduction to the video's topic and demonstration of the initial operating system (Windows 8.1).
The speaker announces his intention to show how to upgrade from Windows 8 to Windows 10.
The speaker shows the control panel and confirms the presence of Windows 8.1.

videoEditingDetails.description: Introductory title card with the text 'Tutor Terrific' appears.
Transition to a desktop view.
The Windows 8.1 Start menu and control panel are shown.
Transition to the Microsoft website for downloading Windows 10.

activities.description: Explanation of the Microsoft website and download tool.

narrativeProgression.description: The speaker guides the viewer through the process of downloading the Windows 10 installation tool.
The speaker explains that the downloaded file is the installation media.

videoEditingDetails.description: The Microsoft website is shown.
The speaker emphasizes the importance of the link, which is included in the video's description.
The 'Download tool now' button is pressed, and the download progress is shown.
The download is complete, and the browser is closed.

narrativeProgression.description: The installation tool begins its work, prompting the user to accept the license terms and choose the desired action.
The speaker highlights the difference between upgrading the current PC and creating installation media for another device.
The 'Upgrade this PC now' option is selected.

videoEditingDetails.description: The downloaded tool file is opened and run.
A 'Getting a few things ready' window appears.
The 'Applicable notices and license terms' window is shown.
The 'What do you want to do?' window is shown, with options for upgrading or creating installation media.

activities.description: Displaying space requirements and prompting to free up space.

narrativeProgression.description: The speaker addresses the importance of having enough disk space and navigates a potential issue with insufficient space.
The speaker emphasizes that 8GB of free space is necessary on the C drive.
The speaker confirms that downloading begins after ensuring enough disk space is available.

videoEditingDetails.description: A window appears, stating that 8GB of free disk space is needed.
The speaker mentions using the built-in disk cleanup tool if needed.
The download progress for Windows 10 is shown.
The download is complete.

activities.description: Cleaning up before closing the tool.

narrativeProgression.description: The downloaded files are verified, Windows 10 media is created, and the system prepares for the final installation.
The speaker assures viewers that the change in the window's message is normal.

videoEditingDetails.description: A window titled 'Verifying your download' appears.
The window title changes to 'Creating Windows 10 media.'
A window pops up saying 'Setup is cleaning up before it closes.'
A small window in the bottom right corner appears, stating 'Preparing Windows' with a progress bar.

activities.description: Accepting the license terms for Windows 10.
Choosing what to keep during the upgrade.

narrativeProgression.description: The speaker accepts the license terms, confirms the upgrade options, addresses space requirements again, and finally initiates the Windows 10 installation.
The speaker acknowledges that the process takes a while due to multiple updates and restarts.
The speaker explains that the prompt for an external drive is due to the limited storage space on the device.
The speaker emphasizes that the PC will be unusable during the installation process.

videoEditingDetails.description: The license terms window appears again for Windows 10.
The 'Choose what to keep' window is shown, with the options to keep personal files and apps.
Another space requirement window appears, prompting the use of an external drive for additional space.
The 'Ready to Install' window appears, summarizing the upgrade choices.

activities.description: Initiating the installation and restarting the PC.
Installing updates after the first restart.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The completion of the upgrade leads to a positive feeling of accomplishment and gratitude.

narrativeProgression.description: The final stage of the upgrade is shown, culminating in a successful installation of Windows 10.
The speaker reassures viewers that multiple restarts are normal.
The speaker confirms the appearance of the Windows 10 loading screen after the final restart.
The speaker highlights that all personal files and programs remain intact after the upgrade.

Transition to a close-up shot of the laptop screen showing the same 'Installing Windows 10' message.
The message changes to 'Keep your PC on until this is done. Installing update 9 of 78...'
The message changes to 'Working on updates' with a progress bar.
Transition to a TV screen showing the Windows 10 logo and loading animation.
The Falconator's hand gives a thumbs-up.
Transition to a white screen with 'Thanks for Watching' and a subscribe button.

youtube_description:
In this video, I go through the entire process, step by step, that allows you to upgrade your operating system from Windows 8 to Windows 10 by yourself, for free!  There is not product key required!

Here is the link to the Windows 10 Download: https://www.microsoft.com/software-download/windows10

INSTALLATION FAILED: I’m seeing a lot of comments about failed installations.  Someone recently discovered a solution: download the install files to a flash drive instead of the hard drive and boot from there during the process.  Just make sure you flash drive is empty (you will lose anything already on there) and has more than 10GB of space (try a 16GB, 32GB, or 64GB flash drive).

NOTE: whatever architecture you currently have, whether it be 32 bit or 64 bit, will remain after you upgrade.  If you are looking to switch from 32 bit to 64 bit, this is not how that is done.

PRODUCT KEY: Originally, Windows would use your existing product key and register your new version of Windows once you log on and connect to the internet.  You did not need to obtain your existing key or purchase a new one.  That still seems to work for some people, but others are required to put in a product key before they’re allowed to continue. Please read the pinned comment in the comment section below for more details if that is your situation.

Please like, comment, and subscribe!
